We investigate problems encountered in the analysis of longitudinal change, where the difference in some outcome variable is modeled on a set of regressor variables in a linear regression model. Previous work demonstrated the effects of measurement error in the analysis of change in wall thickness of the common carotid artery, showing the naive analysis led to erroneous findings due to measurement error bias, even when the regressor variables were assumed to be measured precisely. _**Agent (copilot/auto)**_

Short answer: today, no, not effectively.

What that means:

- The top-level any-llm API accepts arbitrary extra arguments and forwards them:
  - [src/any_llm/api.py](../any-llm/src/any_llm/api.py#L22)
- The Copilot SDK provider receives those extras in kwargs:
  - [src/any_llm/providers/copilotsdk/copilotsdk.py](../any-llm/src/any_llm/providers/copilotsdk/copilotsdk.py#L345)
- But inside that provider, timeout is never read or enforced around:
  - non-streaming wait: [send_and_wait call](../any-llm/src/any_llm/providers/copilotsdk/copilotsdk.py#L392)
  - streaming loop: [queue wait loop](../any-llm/src/any_llm/providers/copilotsdk/copilotsdk.py#L332)

So timeout can be passed in, but the current copilotsdk provider implementation does not apply it. In practice, it behaves as unsupported/ignored for that provider.

If you want, I can patch any-llm so timeout is actually enforced for both non-streaming and streaming paths.
